gate: Somewhere under the breastbone of a person carrying this code is the old job of the chief at the fire. Counting the people. Naming what the group has and where it is heading and how it will keep itself fed through the winter. The pull lands in the throat as a need to speak that count aloud, to put the gathering into words the gathered can stand under. It is not a wish to dominate anyone. It is a built-in sense of responsibility for the people who have collected around this life, voiced as direction. The misread is to call this bossiness, or to flatten it into ambition for status. The drive underneath is older than any office. Denied a tribe to speak for, it can curdle into hoarding, or into a loud insistence on being heard for its own sake. Given the right room, the voice settles into a quiet, certain authority that the people around it want to follow.
centre_field: The drive here is wired to the throat, the body's loudspeaker, the place where everything inside a person has to turn into a word before it can land in another ear and become a thing in the world. More energy converges on this one part of you than on any other. Whatever you carry, it is rushing here to be voiced. That is the whole teaching. Leadership in this code is not a private feeling of authority a person walks around holding. It is the spoken kind. The gatherer who never names the gathering has not actually led anything yet. The cost of misusing this seat shows up in the body. Burned-out voice, burned-out thyroid, the body's plain way of saying it was pushed to speak when it should have rested. The voice is precious cargo, and the timing of its use is half of what makes the leading work.
channel: Knowing how to speak for the group is only half of what makes a working leader. A voice that announces direction without knowing what the people actually have in their stores is a rallying speech with nothing behind it. This code reaches for its other half in the part of you that counts the resources, the inward steward who keeps track of what is in the kitchen and what can actually be spent. Joined, the two make the working tribal leader, the one who can name what the people have and direct how it gets used. Alone, this code is announcement without ledger, a head of the table with no idea what is in the storehouse. The right to lead comes from being rooted in the count. Without that grounding, the voice loses what gave it standing in the first place.
